Salesforce: Gradual and Steady Upward Revenue Trends

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) primarily generates revenue by offering an integrated suite of cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) software that helps large global enterprises manage their complex daily sales pipelines, analyze marketing data, facilitate internal team collaboration, and automate essential customer support operations.

It recently completed the acquisition of customer AI agent platform Fin, and it entered a definitive agreement to purchase customer engagement platform Braze for an estimated enterprise value of $5.66 billion.

International Business Machines: Higher Yet Fluctuating Revenue

International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) earns its revenue by delivering open-source hybrid cloud software platforms, managing complex on-premises technology infrastructure, providing working capital financing solutions, and offering specialized business transformation and strategy consulting services to heavily regulated global organizations.

It recently unveiled a next-generation dual-architecture mainframe processor designed specifically for running native applications, while concurrently facing securities fraud investigations initiated by legal firms regarding management representations about new business deals.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue serves as a primary indicator of underlying consumer demand that shows how much total money a business brings in from its core operations before deducting any operating expenses. Tracking this top-line financial figure helps investors understand the total scale and growth trajectory of a business.

NEW YORK, November 03, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Braze (NASDAQ: BRZE), the leading customer engagement platform that empowers brands to Be Absolutely Engaging™, today announced it will release its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, ended October 31, 2026, after U.S. financial markets close on Tuesday, December 8, 2026. From cross-channel messaging and journey orchestration to AI-powered decisioning and optimization, Braze enables companies to turn action into interaction through autonomous, 1:1 personalized experiences. The company has been consistently recognized as a Leader in marketing technology by industry analysts and was named a G2 "Best of Marketing and Digital Advertising Software Product" in 2026. Braze was also named one of Built In's 2026 Best Places to Work, one of America's Greenest Companies for 2025 by Newsweek, and a 2025 Fortune Best Workplace in Technology™ by Great Place To Work®. The company is headquartered in New York with 15 offices across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC. Learn more at Braze.com.

title: Salesforce (CRM) Files Share Offering, Is The Pullback A Valuation Opportunity?
detail:
Salesforce (CRM) Files Share Offering, Is The Pullback A Valuation Opportunity?
Sasha Jovanovic
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 11:17 AM EST 5 min read
CRM
Trade CRM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Salesforce (CRM) has filed a shelf registration to offer 609,118 common shares, worth about US$139.6 million, tied to an employee stock ownership plan. That move puts fresh attention on dilution and compensation.

Salesforce's share price has slipped in the short term, with a 1-day move down 1.3% and a 7-day share price return down 8.65%, even though the 90-day share price return is up 18.43% from earlier levels.

Scan how other AI focused software players are pricing dilution, growth and free cash flow by running the hand picked 40 profitable AI stocks that aren't just burning cash alongside Salesforce in your watchlist.

Bulls point to Salesforce's US$188.6b scale, AI push and growing free cash flow. Bears focus on dilution, acquisitions and a share price that has slipped recently. Which story do the current valuation numbers support next?

Most Popular Narrative: 12% Undervalued

Against a last close of $226.18, the most followed Salesforce narrative pegs fair value at about $255.90. This frames the current pullback as a discount rather than a premium.

The per-seat licence was only ever the toll booth. The asset is the governed system of record: every customer, every deal, every entitlement, for about 80% of the Fortune 500. And the one thing an autonomous AI agent cannot do is act on a customer without getting into that record first. An agent with no permissions, no governance and no audit trail is not an asset, it is a liability waiting to happen. So the same automation wave that threatens the seat count is exactly what drives every serious enterprise deeper into the data layer Salesforce owns. The meter changes from per-person to per-action. It does not disappear.

See why 41 investors see Salesforce as 12% undervalued.

The narrative, according to michaelyang, anchors on a discount rate of 9% and a fair value that sits around 11.6% above that quoted figure. That framing leans heavily on Salesforce earning power from a $43.9b top line, $9.7b of net income and the idea that a governed data layer can keep monetisation intact even if traditional seat based pricing shifts.

It also leans on history. The storyteller highlights revenue growth of 8.9% a year and profit expansion of 43.7% a year over five years as evidence that the business model adapted through previous shifts in software spending. In that context, a forecast revenue growth rate of 9% a year that trails the wider US market at 13.1% a year is presented as conservative, not aggressive.

Not every datapoint reinforces the optimistic side. The same narrative acknowledges a one off $3.5b gain that flatters the latest twelve month earnings, high leverage that influences a 25.18% return on equity, and a funding mix that relies entirely on higher risk borrowing rather than customer deposits. Those factors sit alongside concerns about insider selling in the last quarter and a one year total return that trailed both the US market and the US software sector.

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) traded at $219.20, down 3.09% at 10:15 a.m. ET on November 3, as its agreement to acquire Cresta put voice AI in focus. The customer relationship management software provider aims to connect AI-powered customer conversations with Service Cloud workflows. The Next Web reported that Salesforce did not disclose the purchase price, leaving investors without a key number for assessing the deal's economics. The decline coincided with the acquisition news, although that does not establish the transaction as its sole driver.

Salesforce's announcement outlines a platform spanning voice agents, real-time support for human representatives and conversation analysis. Cresta's customers include Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines, giving Salesforce an established deployment base to build on. Closing is expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2028, subject to required approvals and other conditions. The commercial test could be turning those capabilities into paid adoption across Salesforce's service business.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a GF Score of 89 out of 100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 19.98, with stronger readings for growth and profitability than for financial strength and GF Value. That suggests business quality deserves attention, but does not settle whether the acquisition will earn an attractive return. Salesforce needs to show that voice automation can resolve more customer problems, support retention and cover model-running costs. Integration and measurable revenue gains could matter more than the customer roster alone.

title: Should You Buy Salesforce Stock For Its Cash?

Should You Buy Salesforce Stock For Its Cash?

Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Salesforce (CRM) trade 38.5% below their December 4, 2024 high, making the company's cash generation worth examining. Over the last twelve months, Salesforce generated free cash flow equal to 8.2% of its market value, compared with 4.2% for the median S&P 500 company. Cash priced this cheaply points to either a fundamentally sound business trading at a discount or a company that investors expect to shrink. So which of the two is Salesforce?

Salesforce Has Grown Its Free Cash Flow Every Year

Salesforce fits the profile of a sound business trading at a discount. Measured a year apart, the company has increased its free cash flow in each of the last three years, reaching $15.2 billion in the twelve months to July 31, 2026, up from $7.56 billion three years earlier.

This cash holds value for shareholders regardless of whether management pays it out, since an owner retains a claim on it just as they do on earnings. Cash kept inside the company still belongs to its investors. Over time, a share price often follows that cash, particularly when the cash is growing, though Salesforce shares have not done so yet.

The company sells subscription software, ranging from Agentforce Service and Agentforce Sales to Slack, and running this business requires minimal capital. Capital spending accounted for 3.8% of cash from operations over the last twelve months. Revenue over that period reached $43.9 billion, an 11.2% increase from a year earlier. The operating margin widened to 21.5%, up from 19.1% two years before.

The business must now service a larger debt load. Total debt stood at $41.7 billion on July 31, 2026, compared with $11.2 billion a year earlier. Over the same twelve months, Salesforce repurchased $35.1 billion of its own shares. Measured against enterprise value, which combines market value with debt net of cash, free cash flow equals 7.0%.

Why Do Investors Doubt Salesforce's Subscription Business?

The current share price suggests AI will reduce corporate demand for Salesforce subscriptions. Management addressed this doubt during its August 26, 2026 call, noting that skeptics expected seat counts to decline and customers to leave. Executives strongly refuted concerns of a structural downturn in software demand.

Some results align with those concerns. Revenue in the Agentforce Marketing and Agentforce Commerce segment grew 2.8% in fiscal 2026, slowing from 7.5% the year before. During the call, management also said licensed revenue remained volatile.
